# dsh-session-copy
English | 中文

One button in the DSH Web session header. Click it and pick what to copy —
**deep link**, **whole co

nversation as Markdown**, **only the messages you tick**,
or **working directory**. No more row of f
lat buttons competing with the toolbar.
## Why this exists

The session header is a crowded strip of icon buttons, and copying a conversation
out of DSH used to

mean three of them. This plugin folds the three into one
28-pixel button whose menu carries the sam

e actions, so the header gains nothing
but a single icon.

The one that actually takes work is **Markdown**. A session log is not a chat
transcript: it is a st

ream of tool calls, retries, pruned rows, injected context
and — after a while — compaction checkpoi

nts. This plugin reconstructs the
conversation from that stream on the Host side and hands back clea

lugin reconstructs the
conversation from that stream on the Host side and hands back clean Markdown.
## What you get
| Menu item | What you get |
| **Copy deep link** | `@title>)` — the canonical DSH session mention. Paste it into any composer an

d the Host attaches that session's snapshot, so another conversation can read this one. |
| **Copy M
arkdown** | The whole conversation as clean Markdown on the clipboard: one section per message, ever
y assistant step kept, tool output and reasoning folded away, compaction points marked, code fences

balanced. |
| **Export Markdown file** | The same document saved as a `.md` file. Use this for anyth

ing long — a clipboard write is the part that fails first, and the file has no length cap. |
| **Sel
ect messages…** | Opens a timeline picker; tick the messages you want and copy or export only those

— the QQ/WeChat multi-select gesture. |
| **Copy directory** | The session's `cwd`, read from the Se
ssion list projection with the Host snapshot as fallback. |

Every action reports back in a small notice — including the character count, so
you can tell a 400-c
haracter session from a 400,000-character one.
## Why there is a file export

A clipboard write is the weakest link in "copy the whole conversation": browsers
cap or refuse a sin

gle write of a few hundred kilobytes, and a silent truncation
looks like the plugin lost your histor
y. Measured on a real 4.3 MB session log:
| | Characters | Complete? |

| Clipboard copy (capped) | 212,330 | no — trimmed at the cap |
| File export | 778,435 | yes |

So the clipboard action keeps its cap and says when it trims, while the export
action asks the Host

to lift it (8,000,000 characters, still finite so a corrupt
log cannot exhaust memory) and hands you

the file. The picker has the same pair
of buttons: **Copy** and **Export .md**.
## Picking only part of a conversation

A long session usually has one stretch worth sharing: the debugging thread, the
decision, the answer

. **Select messages…** opens a timeline of every message
with its role, a one-line preview and its s
ize, and copies only what you tick.

- **Timeline.** The list is grouped by turn; each group has a sticky header with
the turn number, it

s **calendar date** and time range, and its size, and a rail
down the left marks every turn — click

a marker to jump to it, and the active
marker follows your scrolling. Every row shows the time its m

essage was sent.
- **Oldest / Newest** switches the whole timeline around, rail included, so you
can

start from the most recent exchange when the part you want is recent. The
order never changes *whic

h* message a tick refers to.
- **Whole turn** on a header ticks (or clears) every message in that ex

change,
which is usually the unit you actually want.
- **Role chips** — All / You / Assistant / Comp

action — cut the list down to the
side you want; only the roles actually present are offered.
- **Fi

lter** narrows hundreds of rows to the ones you are after. Both the filter
and the chips scope **Sel

ect all**, so "every question I asked about the
parser" is one chip plus one word.
- **Shift-click**

selects a whole range, the way a chat app does, and a range
never escapes the current filter.
- **K

eyboard**: `Space` toggles the focused row, `↑`/`↓`/`Home`/`End` move
between rows, `Ctrl`/`⌘+A` tic

ks everything visible, `Escape` closes.
- The meter reads `4 of 7 · 1,832 characters` — both the cou

nt and the size of
what you are about to paste.
- The copied document opens with `> Excerpt: 12 of 3

40 messages selected`, so a
pasted fragment is never mistaken for a truncated export.
- The picker i

ncludes the complete history: compaction checkpoints appear as
their own rows, so an intentional sum

mary can be included or left out on
purpose.
- Selecting is local to the dialog — nothing is copied

until you press
**Copy**. Opening it again refreshes the list, so messages added while the
picker wa
s closed are not hidden by stale data.

### Inside the desktop app

The desktop app has its own plugin manager: open **Settings → Plugins** and
install from there, rath

er than with the CLI (which targets a different profile
while the app is running). Then restart Deep

Seek Harness — the Loader assembles
its plugin list at boot, so a reload of the page is not enough.

The asset name is deliberately version-free. A `releases/latest/download/` URL
resolves `latest` at

request time but takes the filename literally, so a
versioned filename would work until the next rel

ease and then quietly 404; the
[该节后续省略]
## Compatibility
| Host | DSH `0.2.1-rc.2` and newer (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` peers are pinned to the prerelease branche

s) |
| Surface | DSH Web and the desktop app's Web view |
| Permissions | none — the Host route is r
ead-only and same-origin fenced |

Everything is feature-detected against the shared client module table. If a future
DSH release drops

the `Menu` primitive, the menu still renders in a
self-contained popover; if it renames a service,

the affected piece degrades
rather than raising inside the boot activation audit.
